title: Before an optimisation run, show the design space; during it, show the cost; when it fails, show the log
summary: Three views of one demo optimisation run: where the target conditions sit in temperature, pressure and equivalence ratio, the running tool with an empty cost pane, and the log of the failure that stopped it. The reading skills are standard: coverage of a design space, what a progress panel must show, and how to read a traceback.

media.alt: A 3D scatter titled T-P-phi space with temperature in kelvin from about 950 to 1040, pressure in pascals from 0 to 300000, and an equivalence ratio axis with ticks 2, 4 and 6. Five coloured points are visible on a light grey 3D grid, coloured by phi from dark purple (low) to yellow (6); a single yellow point sits at the upper left.

read_the_figure.question: Do the target conditions cover the space the optimiser will be judged on, is the run progressing, and if it stopped, why?
read_the_figure.axes: Design-space plot: x temperature in K (ticks 960 to 1040), y pressure in Pa (0 to 300,000), z equivalence ratio phi (ticks 2, 4, 6); colour is phi again (0 to 6). Tool screenshots: banner, a configuration field naming the run file, a Cost / errors pane (empty), a Log pane, and a status line.
look_at: Design space: count the distinct markers (five) and compare with the caption's 30 targets: several targets share the same condition and their markers overlap.
Note how narrow the temperature axis is (960 to 1040 K, about 80 K wide) and how widely phi varies (to 6): the targets cover mixture strongly and temperature weakly.
Running screenshot: the Cost / errors pane is empty and the log has one line, 15:11:28 Run started. No progress curve exists yet.

Error screenshot: read the last lines of the log from the bottom: FileNotFoundError: No such file or directory: 'nominal/case-7', above it the code line os.chdir("nominal/case-" + str(case)), and a pointer to the full log in /tmp.
read_the_figure.proves: That the run reached the sensitivity step and stopped on a missing directory from a prerequisite run, and that the targets sit in a narrow temperature window. It says nothing about optimiser quality, since no cost was ever plotted.
if_wrong: A 3D scatter of a few points cannot reveal exact coordinates: perspective hides depth. Use projections.
Overlapping points hide counts: use size or jitter, or print the number of targets per point.
A cropped window that overlaps another can be read as one: ignore the strip at the bottom of these screenshots, which is part of another window.
must_check: The plot shows every target (or states multiplicity).
Axes have units and readable labels (the pressure and phi labels overlap ticks here).
A progress panel plots error against iteration on a log axis with the best-so-far, not a single number.
A failure is shown together with its cause and the fix.
File paths in a screenshot are meaningful to the reader or described in the caption.
as_drawn: Temperature ticks from 960 to 1040 K; pressure ticks 0 to 300,000 Pa (about 3 atm); phi up to 6, with one point at the top of the phi range.
Log: Run started at 15:11:28; the error is a FileNotFoundError for the relative path nominal/case-7.

terms.meaning: The set of conditions (here T, P, phi) at which the targets are defined. An optimiser is judged on how well it fits them, so their coverage matters.
Repeated evaluation of an objective while parameters are changed to reduce it. The cost per evaluation and the number of evaluations set the total time.
A population-based search that keeps and recombines the best candidates over successive generations.
A live plot of the objective against iteration, usually the best so far and the population spread.
The list of calls leading to an error. The last line is the error; the line above it is where it was raised.
A file path interpreted from the current working directory, as in nominal/case-7. It fails if the program starts elsewhere or the folder was never created.
A step whose output the next step reads. Here the optimisation's sensitivity sub-step expects a nominal-simulation case folder.

remember: Read a traceback from the bottom: error type and message first.
A relative path depends on where the program runs; an absolute path or a check for the folder avoids this class of error.
Overlapping points in a scatter hide counts.
Total optimiser cost is evaluations times the cost per evaluation.
A progress panel without a curve is not evidence of progress.

understand.title: What the design-space plot is for
understand.text: It is generated before any fitting starts. It answers: which conditions will the optimiser's result be judged on? A narrow temperature window, as here, means the fitted result is only tested near 1000 K, even though the mixture spans lean to rich.

understand.title: What the running screenshot shows
understand.text: The Cost / errors pane is the place where the objective should appear against iteration. In this frame it is empty because the run has just started and the log has one line. A reader should not infer progress from it.

understand.title: What the error screenshot teaches
understand.text: The run stopped when a step looked for the folder nominal/case-7, which a previous step should have created. The error is a dependency between two tools, not a bug in the optimiser. Showing it is useful: it documents which prerequisite a user must satisfy.

steps.title: Cost of an optimiser run
steps.note: Each candidate needs one simulation per target. Cutting generations or targets cuts the run time in proportion.

steps.title: Reduction used for a demo
steps.note: The page description says generations were cut from 20,000 to 5 and targets from 426 to 30. The product is the factor by which the demo is cheaper than a full run (computed; the numbers are from the page text, not the screenshots).

steps.title: Distinct points in the design space
steps.note: A scatter draws one marker per unique condition. Five markers for 30 targets means several targets share a condition.

steps.title: What a progress panel should plot
steps.note: The best-so-far curve of an elitist search never rises. A curve that rises means the best was not kept, or the objective changed.

steps.title: Reading an error from the bottom
steps.note: Start at the last line. FileNotFoundError says the path does not exist; the code line shows which path was built; the log pointer tells you where the rest is.

steps.title: Why a relative path is fragile
steps.note: The program resolves the path against the current working directory. If the earlier step wrote its outputs elsewhere, or never ran, the path is missing. Checking existence before changing directory, or passing absolute paths, makes the failure explicit.

worked.title: How much cheaper is the demo run?
worked.problem: Per the project page the demo used 5 generations instead of 20,000 and 30 targets instead of 426. By what factor is the work reduced?

solution.text: Targets per candidate, then the product.

worked.answer: About 57,000 times less work, assuming the population size is unchanged.

analyze.q: Five markers for 30 targets. What are two explanations, and which extra output of the pipeline would tell them apart?
analyze.hint: Repeated conditions with different targets (ignition and flame speed) versus a plotting issue.

analyze.q: The log says 'Run started' and the cost pane is empty. List three things that could be true at that moment.
analyze.hint: Initial evaluation under way; stuck; failed silently.

analyze.q: The error is raised in a line that changes directory. What is the logical dependency between the two tools?
analyze.hint: One writes case folders, the other reads them.

evaluate.q: Is it good practice to publish a screenshot of a failure? Argue both sides and take a position.
Rank the three screenshots by how much each tells a reader about the quality of the optimisation.

create: Design the finished Cost / errors pane: axes, scales, the best-so-far line and the population band.
Rewrite the error message so a user knows what to do without reading the code.

checks.q: Why is the last line of a traceback the most informative?
checks.answer: It names the exception and its message, here FileNotFoundError and the missing path, so it says what went wrong; the lines above say where.

checks.q: A population of 50 for 100 generations with 30 targets at 2 s per simulation: how long is the run, in hours?
checks.answer: 300,000 s, which is about 83 hours (single core, no parallelism).

checks.q: Why does a best-so-far curve never rise in an elitist search?
checks.answer: Because the best candidate is carried to the next generation, the minimum over all generations so far cannot increase.

checks.q: The design space has points only between 960 and 1040 K. What can the optimised model be claimed to fit?
checks.answer: Only conditions near that window; claims beyond need other targets.

checks.q: How would you make the missing-folder error informative?
checks.hint: A check with a clear message.
checks.answer: Test that the folder exists before using it and raise an error that names the missing folder and the step that should have created it.
